items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I had a friend, Lloyd Reese, and one day he said, "You know, Jim, I know how you think, but please don't use that word anymore."

ctx.x: So I do know a little bit about prejudice but I know

I myself used the word "nigger," not knowing that was a bad term until years later. I had a friend, Lloyd Reese, and one day he said, "You know, Jim, I know how you think, but please don't use that word anymore." I said, "What's wrong with it?" He said, "That's not a good word." I said, "What do you mean it's not a good word? What should I say?" He said, "Well, call us Negroes or even call us Oxford Grays, but don't call us niggers." And I wanted to die, you know. I sank into the ground. So then I spent the next…

In junior college I had this black guy I used to wrestle with and box. And I did know about prejudice because I was a little surprised at junior college, he was sort of in with this bunch of guys, musicians and sort of like a hep crowd there that I was with, being a musician. And we would all go to the dances together and I remember we would dance with his girlfriend and he would dance with white girls and I do remember I was surprised. So I did know a little about prejudice.
